steps.title: Perpendicular
steps.instruction: Perpendicular lines meet at a right angle. Rotating a line 90° about a point on it produces a perpendicular line through that point.

questions.prompt: Line C and its 90° rotation C′ intersect at (6, 5). Line C passes through (−2, 9); line C′ passes through (0, −7).
hints: Use two points on each line: slope = (y₂ − y₁) ÷ (x₂ − x₁).
Line C: from (−2, 9) to (6, 5). Line C′: from (0, −7) to (6, 5).
Then use y = mx + b and one point to find b.

questions.prompt: Worked example, then you prove it. Line p passes through O(0, 0) and R(a, b), so its slope is m₁ = b/a. Rotate R 90° CLOCKWISE about O to get point D on line q.

responses.label: The slope of line q is m₂ = …
This proves that the slopes of perpendicular lines are …

hints: A 90° clockwise rotation sends (x, y) to (y, −x).
Slope from O(0, 0) to D(b, −a) is (−a − 0)/(b − 0).
Multiply b/a by −a/b.

steps.title: Theorem
steps.instruction: If two lines are perpendicular, their slopes are negative reciprocals: m₁ = −1/m₂, so m₁·m₂ = −1 (neither line vertical).

steps.title: Counterclockwise version
steps.instruction: Rotating R(a, b) 90° counterclockwise gives D(−b, a), so m₂ = a/(−b) and m₁ = b/a = −1/m₂.

steps.title: Rise over run
steps.instruction: Slope = rise ÷ run. A horizontal line has a rise of 0, so its slope is 0 ÷ run = 0. A vertical line has a run of 0, and division by 0 is undefined.
